newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS confirms talks for Thai firm control.
newsitem.headline: DBS confirms talks for Thai firm control.

text.p: The Development Bank of Singapore (DBS) said on Thursday it has had discussions with the Srivikorn Family on taking a majority stake in Sri Dhana Finance and Securities Plc.

DBS said in a statement: "we have had discussions with the Srivikorn Family with a view to taking a majority stake" in Sri Dhana. DBS gave no other details, but said further announcements would be made as and when appropriate.
Earlier on Thursday a senior central bank official in Thailand said DBS was set to take a 60 percent stake in Sri Dhana.
The proposed deal follows Thailand's recent easing of rules on foreign equity participation and the central bank approved the proposal in principle, he said.
"It is a welcome development which is in line with the central bank's policy," he said.
Sri Dhana, of which DBS now holds about 10 percent, was one of 10 finance companies ordered by the Bank of Thailand in March to increase its capital.
But it was not included in the list of 16 ailing finance companies the authorities suspended recently and ordered to merge or consolidate with stronger ones.

Thai financial authorities, in a move to attract foreign inflows to avert a financial meltdown, had recently issued decrees allowing foreign investors to hold more than a 25 percent stake in finance firms.
The central bank had sent a strong signal that it wanted the sector to consolidate through mergers and acquisitions and let the financially distressed ones go under.
